what_happens_to_the_case: The caller gets no answer: connection refused or no instance to route to. The move fails back or is retried by the caller
how_it_is_usually_seen: caller errors naming the callee; callee instance count or health

what_happens_to_the_case: The callee answers with a failure. The move fails back unless the caller retries
how_it_is_usually_seen: caller and callee errors for the operation

what_happens_to_the_case: The move waits on the callee. With no deadline the case waits as long as the caller does
how_it_is_usually_seen: caller duration; requests in flight; the callee's own duration
practice: RED: duration; Four Golden Signals: latency, saturation

what_happens_to_the_case: A deadline or a cancelled request ends the call. Work the callee already did may stand while the case is reported failed
how_it_is_usually_seen: caller cancellation or deadline errors; callee work with no matching caller success
practice: gRPC deadlines and cancellation; Nygard, Release It!: timeouts

what_happens_to_the_case: The publisher cannot hand the message to the broker. The move does not start unless something re-sends
how_it_is_usually_seen: publisher errors at publish; the broker unreachable from the publisher
practice: Hohpe and Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Guaranteed Delivery

what_happens_to_the_case: The broker accepts the message but no queue receives it (nothing bound). It is dropped
how_it_is_usually_seen: broker unroutable or returned-message counts; a consumer queue that receives nothing
practice: Enterprise Integration Patterns: Dead Letter Channel

what_happens_to_the_case: The message waits in the queue. The move happens when a consumer returns
how_it_is_usually_seen: queue depth growing; no consumer attached to the queue
practice: Enterprise Integration Patterns: Competing Consumers; USE: saturation

what_happens_to_the_case: The consumer throws. The message is redelivered or discarded depending on how the consumer acknowledges
how_it_is_usually_seen: consumer error logs naming the message; redelivery or dead-letter counts
practice: Enterprise Integration Patterns: Dead Letter Channel; poison message

what_happens_to_the_case: Messages wait longer than the design assumes. The move happens late
how_it_is_usually_seen: queue depth and consumer lag growing while the consumer runs

what_happens_to_the_case: The state change committed but its outbox row was never relayed (a crash or a lost connection between commit and publish). The move out never starts
how_it_is_usually_seen: outbox rows still in their initial state older than a relay cycle

what_happens_to_the_case: The relay tried and recorded a failure. Whether it tries again depends on the relay
how_it_is_usually_seen: outbox rows in a failed state

what_happens_to_the_case: Nothing reads the outbox. Every change waits
how_it_is_usually_seen: no outbox row published since a point in time; the relay process absent

what_happens_to_the_case: Nothing picks the cases up. Every case waits in the polled state
how_it_is_usually_seen: no poll activity; the poller process absent
practice: Scheduler and batch job monitoring: missed runs

what_happens_to_the_case: The poller runs but cannot read the cases it should move
how_it_is_usually_seen: poller errors on its query

what_happens_to_the_case: The poller runs and reads but its selection misses cases (a filter or clock value)
how_it_is_usually_seen: cases older than the poll's own bound still in the polled state while the poller reports runs
practice: Scheduler monitoring: run with no effect

what_happens_to_the_case: The case waits past the time the design assumes
how_it_is_usually_seen: cases past the timer's bound still waiting

what_happens_to_the_case: The case waits a different time than before because the setting changed
how_it_is_usually_seen: configuration history; the wait distribution shifting at a change

what_happens_to_the_case: The act throws inside the service. Its transaction rolls back and the case stays where it was
how_it_is_usually_seen: service error logs or spans for the operation

what_happens_to_the_case: The act completes and records a wrong outcome for the case
how_it_is_usually_seen: a check of the case's recorded values against the right outcome

what_happens_to_the_case: The case waits for a person or outside party who is not told or not assigned
how_it_is_usually_seen: cases waiting on the person past the time the business expects
practice: Workflow and case management: unassigned work

what_happens_to_the_case: The person acts and the case records a wrong outcome
how_it_is_usually_seen: a check of the case's recorded values against the right outcome

what_happens_to_the_case: A store; broker or outside service the move needs does not answer. The move fails or waits
how_it_is_usually_seen: the part's own availability and error measures; callers' errors naming it

what_happens_to_the_case: The part answers late. The move waits
how_it_is_usually_seen: the part's own latency and saturation

what_happens_to_the_case: The part refuses work for lack of capacity (connections; disk; queue limit)
how_it_is_usually_seen: the part's saturation and utilization
